quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Always look ahead and expect possible dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because there are very few on the road.
Always look ahead, but try not to look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and expect possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead of your motorcycle to help you see hazards before you reach them. This gives you time to react safely.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT protect you in a crash?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: Riders should wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on motorcycles:

options.text: Does not help at all.
Lets the engine help slow down the motorcycle.
Is against the law.
Should not be done around other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets the engine help slow down the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Engine braking by downshifting smoothly is useful for slowing down. If you use engine braking, apply your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Not use your rearview mirrors to check traffic behind you.
Look for gaps to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when both are stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or another vehicle comes too close from behind.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still feel the effects of the alcohol.
You will be safe as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still feel the effects of the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink's worth of alcohol per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your body. Your ability to ride safely and your judgment can still be impaired.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden on a motorcycle before.
Not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
Not let them ask questions.
Not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: Passengers need to know how to ride safely. Never assume they have ridden a motorcycle before. Give clear instructions before every ride.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Protect only your eyes.
Work as well as a face shield.
Give the same protection as a windshield.
Protect your entire face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect only your eyes.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only, not your face. A face shield protects your entire face and is better than goggles. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Safe when used correctly.
Safe even if used incorrectly.
Only for use if the rear brake fails.
Not meant for regular use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safe when used correctly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used properly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least three-fourths of the total stopping power.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always stay there.
Move around the lane constantly to keep other drivers away.
Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: If your motorcycle will take longer than usual to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.
Leave the road.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle takes longer to stop. This gives you more time and space to react safely.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Sturdy boots
Tennis shoes
Shoes with loose laces
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or high-top shoes that support your ankles. Laced-up boots work best. Make sure any long laces are tucked away before riding.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder
Ride below the speed limit
Wear a helmet
Do not carry a passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single best way to protect your head and neck in a crash.

questions.question: What should you do before carrying a passenger on your motorcycle?

options.text: Prepare your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way as you do alone.
Remove the passenger footrests.
Teach the passenger while you are riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a large enough seat for two people, separate footrests for the passenger, and may need adjustments to the headlight, tires, and suspension to handle the extra weight.

questions.question: What is a simple way to make your motorcycle more visible to other drivers?

options.text: Attach a large flag to your motorcycle.
Ride with your headlight on.
Wave at other drivers.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on at all times. Also use your turn signals and brake light. Wear bright, reflective clothing.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike since all bikes are the same.
Check where the controls are and learn the gear pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where everything is located.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check where the controls are and learn the gear pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding. Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It allows clear vision to the sides.
It limits your side vision.
It is usually uncomfortable.
It has no labels or markings.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows clear vision to the sides.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet lets you see clearly to the sides for safe riding. All approved helmets have labels showing the manufacturer's name and the safety standards they meet.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Clothing that covers your arms and legs completely.
Clothing that covers your arms but leaves your legs exposed.
Clothing that covers your legs but leaves your arms exposed.
Whatever is most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that covers your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely for proper protection.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?

options.text: A jacket
Boots
Gloves
A stocking cap

questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap
questions.explanation: Protective clothing includes sturdy pants, jackets, boots that support your ankles, and gloves. A stocking cap is not protective motorcycle gear.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required on a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: An impact-resistant outer shell.
An impact-absorbing inner liner.
A chinstrap retention system.
Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system. Bright paint colors are not required.

questions.question: What should you wear to help other drivers see you?

options.text: Dark-colored clothes.
Bright-colored clothes.
Lights.
A black jacket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: Bright clothing makes you easier to see. Wear clothes that stand out during the day and at night.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire and guess.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare it to another tire's height.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check pressure before riding. A tire can look fine but still be under-inflated, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: Which item is NOT required on a street-legal motorcycle?

options.text: A headlight
Turn signals
Two mirrors
A windshield

questions.correctAnswerText: A windshield
questions.explanation: Street-legal motorcycles must have a headlight, taillight, brake light, front and rear brakes, turn signals, a horn, and two mirrors. A windshield is not required.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle blind spots?

options.text: Motorcycles do not have blind spots because they are small.
Blind spots are so small they are not a concern.
You should regularly check for blind spots.
Motorcycles are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should regularly check for blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a regular part of your driving routine.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see and be seen better.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see and be seen better.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It also helps you avoid wind gusts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.
